4. The suit land was then recorded first in the name of Chan Miah in RS Khatian and then as khas in the name of the government. Defendant No. 2 Additional Divisional Commissioner (Revenue) served a notice dated 30-12-90 upon the husband of the plaintiff asking him to vacate the land by 30-1-91 otherwise he would be evicted therefrom by removal of unauthorised structures. Such notice cast a doubt over the title of the plaintiff who was accordingly, constrained to institute the suit. 

 5. Defendant No. 2 alone contested the suit by filing a written statement. His case, in short, is that the suit land was within Ramchandrapur hat of the erstwhile 'Zaminder.' With the wholesale acquisition of land receiving interest under section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 the suit land vested in the government. RS record of rights accordingly recorded the suit land as khas of the government. The suit land was situated at the periphery of Ramchandrapur Bazaar. By purchase from persons who had no title the plaintiff acquired no right title or interest in the suit land. Husband of the plaintiff got the suit land mutated in collusion with corrupt 'Tahshilder' and such mutation had no legal effect.
